title: health checks diagnostics metrics tracing and OpenTelemetry
concepts: Operational visibility has distinct jobs: health endpoints answer whether a process or dependency is suitable for a particular action; metrics summarize numeric behavior over time; traces connect work across boundaries; logs retain event detail. None replaces the others, and high-cardinality or sensitive data must not be emitted as metric labels or trace attributes.

A health check is an application probe with an explicit purpose and failure policy. Liveness should detect a process that cannot recover, readiness should decide whether it should receive traffic, and startup probes should allow initialization; including every remote dependency in liveness can create restart cascades during an outage.

ASP.NET Core emits built-in diagnostics through System.Diagnostics.Metrics meters and ActivitySource activities. Collectors subscribe to selected meters and sources; an exporter transports collected signals to a backend. .NET 11 aligns built-in HTTP server metrics and traces with required OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic-convention fields, so ASP.NET instrumentation packages are optional for those built-in signals.

OpenTelemetry is an instrumentation and transport standard, not a storage backend. Configure resource identity, sampling, metric readers, exporters, processors, and privacy controls deliberately; avoid duplicate instrumentation when both built-in signals and instrumentation packages observe the same server activity.

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, built-in HTTP server meters and request activities carry the required OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic-convention data. The hosting Activity source adds HTTP attributes by default, resolves conventional-route parameters in http.route, adds error.type to 5xx request-duration measurements, and records unhandled exceptions as standard Activity events without setting StatusDescription. The OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore package is optional for these built-in HTTP signals; teach direct MeterProviderBuilder.AddMeter and TracerProviderBuilder.AddSource subscription, and explain when the package remains useful for its additional instrumentation features.

ASP.NET Core 10 added built-in authentication and authorization metrics, and ASP.NET Core 10 added built-in Blazor component metrics. Present these as available in .NET 10 and later rather than attributing them to .NET 11.

Use the current System.Diagnostics.Metrics and Activity APIs for new .NET instrumentation. EventCounters and DiagnosticSource remain relevant for existing tools and legacy instrumentations, but are not equivalent replacements for new metrics and ActivitySource traces.

The ASP.NET Core health-check abstractions are framework-provided. Third-party checks such as AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HealthChecks are separate community packages; don't imply that their database or UI registrations are built into ASP.NET Core.

scopeExclusions: Generic .NET logging configuration and ILogger API behavior are covered in the logging topic; this manifest addresses telemetry correlation and export integration only.
Distributed system observability architecture, SLIs/SLOs, Prometheus, Grafana, cloud monitoring backends, and collector deployment are covered in architecture and infrastructure topics.

Vendor-specific health-check provider packages and database health-check implementations are external packages; teach package boundaries and representative integration patterns without presenting a mutable third-party API catalog as built-in framework surface.
Application-specific dashboards, alert rules, and incident response policies depend on the deployed backend and service objectives.
